sentences.text: 3 NEWSPAPERS RELATING TO CIVIC ISSUES OF CUTTACK CITY:ACTION TAKEN THEREON 247.

As per order no.244 dated 16.05.2025, 19.06.2025 some news items published in daily newspapers were brought to the notice of the Commissioner, Cuttack Municipal Corporation so also to the Collector & District Magistrate, Cuttack by the High Court Bar Association for necessary action.
(i) One news item was published in the daily Odia newspaper under the heading of SAHARARE SAATASAHA ASURAKHITA KOTHA.

Mr. Shiv Toppo, ADM (General), Cuttack and Nodal Officer has appeared through virtual mode and submitted his report dated 18.06.2025 wherein it is stated that a Committee has been formed comprising of Superintending Engineer, R & B Division-I, Cuttack, City Engineer, CMC,
representative of CDA and Sub- Collector, Sadar, Cuttack to identify the unsafe building structures situated in Cuttack City.

The Committee has already started its work and Superintending Engineer,
R & B Division-I, Cuttack and Superintending Engineer, R & B Division-II, Cuttack furnished a list of twelve numbers of unsafe buildings to the Sub-Collector, Sadar, Cuttack for taking action under the provisions of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 and that it would take some time for the Committee to identify the other dilapidated structures in the City.
List this matter on 14.08.2025.

The ADM, Cuttack and Nodal Officer shall furnish a fresh report regarding the identification of dilapidated structures in the City and action taken by the Sub-Collector, Sadar, Cuttack on the unsafe buildings.
(ii) Another news item was published in the daily Odia newspaper under the heading of BARSHA HELE BUDIBA S.C.B., SISHUBHABAN.

The ADM, Cuttack and Nodal Officer in his report dated 18.06.2025 has annexed the compliance report received from General Manager, WATCO Division, Cuttack wherein it is stated that the drain desilting work inside SCBMCH campus and AHPGIC is nearing completion and 80% work has been completed and the rest will be completed by 30.06.2025.
It is further stated that Cuttack Municipal Corporation has installed 04 nos. of dewatering pump motors to address water logging inside the campus.

A meeting was held on 04.06.2025 in the official chamber of ADM, Cuttack in connection with the compliance of order of this Bench dated 16.05.2025 and the proceeding of the meeting has also been annexed with the report dated 18.06.2025 submitted by ADM, Cuttack and Nodal Officer wherein it is stated that the Administrative Officer, SVPPGIP (Sishubhaban), Cuttack expressed that funds of Rs.8,08,76,900/- has already been approved by the Health & Family Welfare Department, Odisha vide letter No.01402 dated 15.01.2025 for construction of drainage facility inside Sishubhaban and placed to SE, Cuttack (R & B), Division-I.

The said work is to be executed by CMC, Cuttack and the SE, Cuttack (R & B), Division-I vide letter No.3079 dated 21.02.2025 has already requested CMC to provide accounts details to transfer the funds for execution of the said work.

It is further stated that the ADM, Cuttack -cum- Nodal Officer impressed upon the Addl. Commissioner and requested him Registrar (Judicial) vs State Of Odisha & Others .... Opp. ... on 19 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/172822842/

sentences.text: It is further stated that the SE, Cuttack (R & B) Division-I, General Manager, WATCO Drainage Division, Cuttack and City Engineer, CMC, Cuttack instructed to take immediate steps for maintenance and repairing of drainage facility of SCBMCH, Cuttack in order to avoid water logging issues during the ensuing monsoon.
The Commissioner, C.M.C., has submitted the report dated 17.06.2025 wherein it is stated that the internal drainage system of SCBMCH is being maintained and desilted by WATCO, Water Supply.
However, CMC has supplied and installed 4 nos. of pumps with full time operators at SCBMCH campus and near Cancer Institute for dewatering of storm water during heavy rain.
One pump set near casualty, one pump set near Cancer Institute and two pumps near post mortem ward have been installed by the CMC and are also being maintained by the CMC.

It is further stated that regarding dewatering from the campus of Sishu Bhawan that in the previous years, the desilting and cleaning of internal drains of Sishu Bhawan campus was undertaken by the Management of Sishu Bhawan/PWD Division/PHD Division.

But in this year, Cuttack Municipal Corporation is undertaking removal of encroachments adjacent/outside area of the Sishu Bhawan premises and desilting and cleaning work of all the internal drains within the Sishu Bhawan campus.

Accordingly,
a high power VOLVO pump bearing capacity of 24 HP has been installed for dewatering of storm water from the Sishu Bhawan campus during the rain. It is further stated that a 10 HP pump will be provided to the said site, if the same will be required at the time of heavy rain.
There is no discharge point available near Sishu Bhawan area for the existing drain.
The entire internal drainage system will be newly constructed as per the tender invited by Cuttack Municipal Corporation for the purpose.

The learned counsel for the C.M.C. has stated that so far as the construction of drainage network at Sishu Bhawan is concerned, tender notice was issued on 16.06.2025 and the last date for submission of bid is 18.07.2025 and the work order will be issued after complying with codal provision on 01.09.2025 and the drainage network shall be completed by 31.08.2026.

During desilting of drains, cover slabs/fencing are being removed and soon after completion of desilting work, the drains are being covered.

sentences.text: In this news item, it is highlighted as to how labourers even minor boys are engaged in the daunting task of clearance of big drains entering inside it without providing them proper safety gear and without adequate safety measures and no responsible officer of the C.M.C. is monitoring the same and thereby endangering the lives of such manual labourers.

One such incident came to light when a man, balancing himself on a motor tube,
was seen swimming bare body in the main storm water channel (MSWC-I) stretching from Matru Bhawan to Nua Bazar, cleaning the weeds with the help of a bamboo stick and some minor boys were allegedly engaged at the site to remove the weeds from the banks of drains in patent violation of Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act.
Needless to say, ensuring the health and safety of labourers is crucial for productive outcome.
This involves implementing measures to prevent work- related injuries, diseases and hazards.

When the labourers are used to clean the big drains manually,
it very often leads to hazardous conditions and can lead to injuries or fatalities due to toxic fumes and coming in contact with sharp objects like broken glasses, metals and spikes besides poisonous snake in the water bodies.

sentences.text: This Court expects that the inhuman methodology resorted to would be stopped immediately and efforts shall be made to undertake the drain cleaning activities by deploying technologically advanced drain cleaning machines.
Be that as it may, it shall be ensured that there is no violation of the provisions of Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act.

Plan of action to streamline the cleaning process of the drains which is crucial to address the issue of water logging, by adopting the latest technology by way of deployment of suitable machines and training of manpower shall be placed before this Court by the C.M.C.
This aspect shall be considered in the next sitting i.e. on 31.07.2025.

(S.K. Sahoo) Judge (V. Narasingh) Judge 248. Steps Taken For Containing Outbreak of 19.06.2025 "Cholera"
During the course of hearing, attention of this Court was drawn to the news item published in two vernacular odia dailies.

In the backdrop of number of cases relating to outbreak of Cholera being reported in different parts of the State including Cuttack City, the Commissioner, CMC, Mr. Anam Charan Patra as well as ADM, Mr. Shibo Toppo who were present on virtual mode, on being asked about the measures taken, assured this Court that steps have already been initiated to effectively counter the outbreak of Cholera on account of water contamination.

Learned counsel for the WATCO, Mr. Bhuyan who is present in Court and Mr. Baishnv Bhusan Behera, GM(WATCO), Water Supply who joined virtually stated that measures have already been taken by the WATCO in this regard.

During the course of hearing, learned Members of the Bar citing the news item "WARD RE SWASTHYA KARMINKA DEKHA NAHIN" questioned the veracity of the claim of the CMC authorities as well as District Administration with regard to steps taken to arrest the spread of Cholera.

Taking note of such concern expressed across the Board, the CMC Commissioner as well as District Administration who was represented by ADM are directed to work in tandem to ensure that the health workers who are at the disposal of the CDMO as well as the health personnel of the CMC visit each Ward of Cuttack city within the next week and submit a report in this regard to this Court.
While visiting the Wards, they are called upon to contact the concerned lawyer representatives the said area as per the existing list.
The District Administration is at liberty to take such steps as necessary particularly relating to the street vendors so as to maintain hygiene and ensure that there is no surge in cases of Cholera.

The members of the Advocates Committee 19.06.2025 representing Sector-6 CDA brought to the notice of the Court that there is water logging in front of the fish market for the last almost three weeks causing disruption of traffic and untold hardship to the commuters.
The CMC Commissioner, Mr. Anam Charan Patra and the City Engineer, Mr. Atanu Kumar Samant assured this Court to address this issue.

The City Engineer, Mr. Atanu Kumar Samant who was present virtually has undertaken to visit the spot tomorrow (20.06.2025) along with the representatives of the Advocates Committee (Mr. S.P.
Sarangi, Advocate) as well as the representatives of Sector-6 Resident Committee, Mr. B.B.
Choudhury, Advocate and take necessary immediate remedial measures.
And, the steps so taken shall be placed on record by the next date i.e. 03.07.2025.
List this matter on 03.07.2025.

opennyai_summary.facts:
But in this year, Cuttack Municipal Corporation is undertaking removal of encroachments adjacent/outside area of the Sishu Bhawan premises and desilting and cleaning work of all the internal drains within the Sishu Bhawan campus.
The entire internal drainage system will be newly constructed as per the tender invited by Cuttack Municipal Corporation for the purpose.
It is further stated that the desilting work of the drains are being carried out by 3 nos. of sanitation agencies on regular basis throughout the year.
Some of the drains which could not be desilted by the sanitation agencies within the targeted period, the Engineering Section has been assigned to carry out the desilting work of those drains.
In the meantime, the Engineering Section has started the desilting work of the said drains, which is targeted to be completed by the end of June, 2025.
The Commissioner, C.M.C., has submitted the report dated 17.06.2025 wherein it is stated that the removal of garbage is being undertaken on daily basis and CMC has taken all possible steps for covering of open drains so as to prevent any untoward situation.
The Advocates Committee drew the attention of the Court that though the C.M.C. is responsible for drain cleaning and desilting within the city to prevent waterlogging and flooding, especially during monsoon season and they are required to utilize both manual labour and machinery to clear the drains of slit, garbage and other obstruction but it is not being done in all the wards in a regular manner and most of the time after the slit and garbage are removed from the drains, it is not taken away for days together which leads to public inconvenience and unhygienic conditions.

This Court expects that the inhuman methodology resorted to would be stopped immediately and efforts shall be made to undertake the drain cleaning activities by deploying technologically advanced drain cleaning machines.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
During desilting of drains, cover slabs/fencing are being removed and soon after completion of desilting work, the drains are being covered.
One such incident came to light when a man, balancing himself on a motor tube,
was seen swimming bare body in the main storm water channel (MSWC-I) stretching from Matru Bhawan to Nua Bazar, cleaning the weeds with the help of a bamboo stick and some minor boys were allegedly engaged at the site to remove the weeds from the banks of drains in patent violation of Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act.
Needless to say, ensuring the health and safety of labourers is crucial for productive outcome.
This involves implementing measures to prevent work- related injuries, diseases and hazards.
When the labourers are used to clean the big drains manually,
it very often leads to hazardous conditions and can lead to injuries or fatalities due to toxic fumes and coming in contact with sharp objects like broken glasses, metals and spikes besides poisonous snake in the water bodies.
Be that as it may, it shall be ensured that there is no violation of the provisions of Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act.
Plan of action to streamline the cleaning process of the drains which is crucial to address the issue of water logging, by adopting the latest technology by way of deployment of suitable machines and training of manpower shall be placed before this Court by the C.M.C.
In the backdrop of number of cases relating to outbreak of Cholera being reported in different parts of the State including Cuttack City, the Commissioner, CMC, Mr. Anam Charan Patra as well as ADM, Mr. Shibo Toppo who were present on virtual mode, on being asked about the measures taken, assured this Court that steps have already been initiated to effectively counter the outbreak of Cholera on account of water contamination.
Taking note of such concern expressed across the Board, the CMC Commissioner as well as District Administration who was represented by ADM are directed to work in tandem to ensure that the health workers who are at the disposal of the CDMO as well as the health personnel of the CMC visit each Ward of Cuttack city within the next week and submit a report in this regard to this Court.
While visiting the Wards, they are called upon to contact the concerned lawyer representatives the said area as per the existing list.
The District Administration is at liberty to take such steps as necessary particularly relating to the street vendors so as to maintain hygiene and ensure that there is no surge in cases of Cholera.
Since the cleaning of drains is intrinsically connected with supply of safe drinking water which is essential for containing the spread of Cholera, necessary steps in this regard shall be taken within the next three days particularly in the areas relating to Budhithakurani Lane, Chandi Chhak and Raja Bagicha Gada as stated in the caption "NARDAMA JALA, PANI PIPE EKKAKAR" as mentioned in the news item published in the odia daily "Prameya" and also Ward Nos.13, 18 & 19 as stated in "NALAPANI RE BUDI RAHUCHI AIR VALVE" published in the odia daily "The Samaj"
and the same shall form a part of the affidavit to be filed.
